items.description: The boundary module (app/routes/) contains no import of the SQLAlchemy session or any ORM session object
The service module (app/services/) contains no import of any SQLAlchemy ORM class or session — ORM access is confined to the repository layer
No hardcoded database connection string appears anywhere in the application source; DATABASE_URL is read exclusively from the process environment
Filing a stock level via the JSON API for a uuid-suffixed SKU and location returns HTTP 2xx and the stock record is durably stored with the filed quantity and inventory_code
The filing form page renders through <App> at route /stock/file via MemoryRouter initialEntries={["/stock/file"]}
The SKU input field carries a data-testid attribute that can be targeted on the /stock/file page
The location input field carries a data-testid attribute that can be targeted on the /stock/file page
The quantity input field carries a data-testid attribute that can be targeted on the /stock/file page
The inventory_code input field carries a data-testid attribute that can be targeted on the /stock/file page
The submit button carries a data-testid attribute that can be targeted on the /stock/file page
Attempting to insert a stock_records row with a NULL quantity (or NULL sku, location, or inventory_code) is rejected by the database with an IntegrityError

Attempting to persist a stock_records row with a negative quantity via the repository against the real branch database raises a database-level CheckViolation and no row with a negative quantity is stored
The service layer rejects a write whose quantity is negative before the call reaches the database — no negative row is stored and the rejection is signalled by a domain exception from the service
A boundary request with an invalid field value returns an error payload that identifies the specific offending field by name rather than a generic message
The integration test suite connects to the DATABASE_URL environment variable pointing to the paired Lakebase branch and the suite contains no in-memory or mocked database driver

The Alembic migration for stock_records completes a single-step downgrade followed by a single-step upgrade against the real branch database without error (marked @pytest.mark.migration; does not target the base revision on downgrade)

Rows seeded with uuid-suffixed skus into stock_records after the create-table migration runs are present with their original field values after a downgrade and re-upgrade cycle confirms the schema is correctly recreated (data-preservation aspect of the additive migration, delta assertion scoped to the test's own seeded rows)
The boundary layer is declared renders_via: react and all responses from app/routes/ are JSON-encoded payloads
app/routes/ contains no server-side template rendering call (no render_template, Jinja2, or equivalent HTML-rendering invocation)
After filing a stock record via the JSON API, a subsequent GET for that uuid-suffixed SKU and location returns the exact same quantity that was submitted
After filing a stock record via the JSON API, a subsequent GET for that uuid-suffixed SKU and location returns the exact same combined inventory_code that was submitted
The stock retrieval page renders through <App> at route /stock/:sku/:location via MemoryRouter initialEntries={["/stock/SKU-1/LOC-A"]}
The quantity value display element carries a data-testid attribute on the retrieval page at /stock/:sku/:location
The inventory_code value display element carries a data-testid attribute on the retrieval page at /stock/:sku/:location
Filing stock twice via the JSON API for the same uuid-suffixed SKU and location pair returns HTTP 2xx on the second call with no error surfaced
After filing stock twice for the same uuid-suffixed SKU and location pair via the JSON API, querying that pair returns exactly one record reflecting the second submission's quantity
Inserting a second stock_records row with a uuid-suffixed sku already present at the same location raises an IntegrityError and leaves exactly one row in the table for that (sku, location) pair
Two concurrent file requests for the same uuid-suffixed (sku, location) pair complete without producing duplicate rows — exactly one row exists for that pair after both transactions commit
A repeat upsert on an existing uuid-suffixed (sku, location) pair does not change the created_at value of the original row
After filing stock for the same SKU and location pair a second time, the filing form at /stock/file does not display an error element
After a repeat file for the same SKU and location pair, the retrieval page at /stock/:sku/:location displays the updated quantity value
